title: The dust attenuation of star-forming galaxies at z ∼ 3 and beyond: New insights from ALMA observations
question: Does the IRX-beta_UV relation of massive star-forming galaxies at z~3 follow the local M99 relation, and does it evolve toward lower IRX at z~4-6?

data.bands: Band 6 for the z~4-5 comparison sample

what.value: ALMA band-6 fluxes of 19 z~4-5 galaxies (Table 8)

evidence.quote: ALMA band-6 fluxes of the $z\sim4-5$ sample are taken from Table 8 of (cite: Scoville2016).

what.value: L_IR, L_UV, beta_UV of z~5-6 galaxies (Table 1)

evidence.quote: We utilise the $L_{\rm IR}$, $L_{\rm UV}$, and $\beta_{\rm UV}$ estimates of the targets from Table 1 of (cite: Barisic2017)

what.value: ALMA 1.3-mm fluxes of the z~3 sample

recipe.goal: Derive L_IR from ALMA 240 GHz fluxes
recipe.method: Fit single-component modified blackbody to the 240 GHz flux and integrate 8-1000 um
key_parameters: Integrated over 8-1000 um; 3 sigma upper limits for 26 non-detections
assumptions: beta_d=1.5; fiducial T_d=40 K (stack best fit 41.5+-2.5 K); 35 K as alternative

recipe.method: Power-law fit to COSMOS15 photometry over rest-frame 1500-2500 A; L_UV at 1600 A
key_parameters: 3 arcsec aperture photometry, typically >10 data points

recipe.method: MAGPHYS SED fits to optical/NIR, MIPS 24um, PACS 100um and ALMA fluxes

recipe.goal: Stack ALMA images in beta_UV bins
recipe.method: Pixel-wise median stack of ALMA maps in three beta_UV bins and for non-detections; weighted by inverse L_UV; peak flux corrected to total flux using mean of detected sources

recipe.goal: Compare IRX-beta and fit IRX-M* relation, test evolution to z~4-6
recipe.method: Compare with M99 and SMC curves; fit normalisation of IRX-M* with slope fixed to Heinis2013; compare with Scoville2016 and Capak2015/Barisic2017 samples

evidence.quote: A total of 41 of our 67 targets were detected at more than $>3\,\sigma$
we obtain a best-fit dust temperature of $T_d=41.5\pm2.5\,{\rm K}$
The $L_{\rm IR}$ of our detected targets range between $5.9\times10^{11}$ and $5.8\times10^{12}\,L_{\odot}$
The stack reveals a tentative detection with a significance of $\sim4.3\,\sigma$
The offset in normalisation relative to (cite: Heinis2013) is thus $0.24\,{\rm dex}$.

answer_key.quantity: Median IRX offsets from best-fit relation at z~4.3 and z~5.5

evidence.loc: 4.4 The Evolution of IRX–$\beta_{\rm UV}$ Beyond $z=3$
evidence.quote: The median offsets from our best-fit IRX–$M_{\ast}$ relation are $\sim0.31\,{\rm dex}$ and $\sim1.2\,{\rm dex}$ for the samples at $z\sim4.3$ and $z\sim5.5$

not_stated_but_needed: ALMA calibration/imaging details (CASA version, cell size, image size) are deferred to Schinnerer2016
Flux measurement method for individual detections (aperture or peak, noise estimation)
Number of bootstrap resamples and the stack total-flux correction factor
Exact IR SED fit procedure including CMB correction
Source coordinates and individual catalogue values
The UV luminosity-inverse weighting scheme used in stacking is only loosely described
missing_for_reproduction: Bootstrap details and total flux correction
score_reason: Public data and simple recipe, but key processing details are deferred to a companion paper and fitting and stacking details are thin.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric stack IRX results, and a simple recipe, though calibration details must come from Schinnerer2016.
